original_value: Semantic segmentation is an important process of scene recognition with deep learning frameworks achieving state of the art results, thus gaining much attention from the remote sensing community. In this paper, an end-to-end conditional random fields generative adversarial segmentation network is proposed. Three key factors of this algorithm are as follows. First, the network combines generative adversarial network and Bayesian framework to realize the estimation from the prior probability to the posterior probability. Second, the skip connected encoder-decoder network is combined with CRF layer to implement end-to-end network training. Finally, the adversarial loss and the cross-entropy loss guide the training of the segmentation network through back propagation. The experimental results show that our proposed method outperformed FCN in terms of mIoU for 0.0342 and 0.11 on two data sets, respectively.

result.paraphrase: Semantic segmentation is a key part of scene recognition, and with deep learning frameworks reaching state-of-the-art performance, it has attracted considerable attention in remote sensing. This paper proposes an end-to-end conditional random fields generative adversarial segmentation network. The method has three main components. First, it integrates a generative adversarial network with a Bayesian framework to estimate from prior probability to posterior probability. Second, a skip-connected encoder-decoder network is combined with a CRF layer to enable end-to-end training. Third, adversarial loss and cross-entropy loss supervise segmentation network training via back propagation. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperformed FCN in mIoU by 0.0342 and 0.11 on the two data sets, respectively.
